device_selection.title: Polling Settings
device_selection.description:
Newly discovered devices appear disabled and can be enabled in device settings. Configure the general polling parameters:
• Location poll interval: How often to start a new polling cycle (60–3600 seconds)
• Device poll delay: Delay between individual device polls within a cycle (1–60 seconds)

Google Home filter: Enabled by default with keywords nest/google/home/mini/hub/display/chromecast/speaker. Matches substitute Home zone coordinates for Google/Nest/Chromecast detections and debounce repeated "home" updates for 15 minutes. Adjust the keywords here if your devices use different names.

reauth_confirm.description:

Paste the full contents of a new **secrets.json** (generated by running GoogleFindMyTools).

Note: The account email is fixed for this reauthentication; to use a different account, remove and re-add the integration.

settings.title: Options
settings.description:
Adjust location settings:
• Location poll interval: How often to poll for locations (60–3600 seconds)
• Device poll delay: Delay between device polls (1–60 seconds)
• Stale threshold: After this time without updates, tracker state becomes unknown

Google Home Filter:
• Enable to associate detections from Google Home devices with the Home zone
• Keywords support partial matching (comma-separated)
• Example: nest matches Kitchen Nest Mini

data.accuracy_gate_enabled: Discard a coarse fix that would displace a better one
data.secrets_extra_watch_paths: Additional secrets.json watch paths (one per line)

data_description.stale_threshold: After this many seconds without a location update, the tracker state becomes unknown. Use the 'Last Location' entity to always see the last known position. Default: 3900 (65 minutes).
data_description.show_location_age: When enabled (default), a 'location_age' attribute (rounded to 1 minute) is added to each tracker entity. It keeps the age of the last observation and changes only with the next one (for example a new fix, the change to stale, or an availability change). The live age is on the 'Last Seen' sensor of each device, the live status on its 'Location status' sensor.
data_description.speed_gate_enabled: When enabled (default), a location fix that would require physically impossible speed (for example a crowd-sourced report placing the tracker hundreds of km away within seconds) is rejected instead of teleporting the tracker. Own GPS reports always pass. Disable only if legitimate fast movements are being dropped.
data_description.roundtrip_confirm_enabled: When enabled (default), a crowd fix that the speed gate would reject as a teleport is accepted instead if it lands back near the position from just before an earlier accepted long jump, within about 15 minutes. This recovers a legitimate return trip rather than leaving the tracker stranded at the far position. It only ever applies where the speed gate would otherwise reject. Disable if you see the tracker flapping between two places.
data_description.accuracy_gate_enabled: When enabled (default), an incoming location fix is discarded if it lies clearly outside the uncertainty circle of the cached position, is at least four times less accurate than it, at least 200 m coarse, and that cached position is both reliable and still fresh. Nothing is ever discarded without a better alternative: a coarse fix is always accepted on a cold start, or when the cached position is unreliable or stale. This stops a wide crowd-sourced report from moving the tracker and - because Home Assistant uses the accuracy radius as the zone tolerance - from falsely reporting it as home. Disable only if you suspect this gate itself is causing a problem. A discarded fix is shown by the device's 'Discarded coarse fix' sensor until a fix that is as new or newer is accepted, the discarded fix is older than the stale threshold, or the integration is reloaded (as on a Home Assistant restart); the rest of the time that sensor shows unknown, which is normal.
data_description.delete_caches_on_remove: Remove cached tokens and device metadata when this entry is deleted.
data_description.map_view_token_expiration: When enabled, map view tokens expire after 1 week. When disabled (default), tokens do not expire.
data_description.map_view_enabled: Enabled by default. When disabled, Map View requests are refused like an invalid token and device links are cleared. Does not rotate existing share links; if one may have leaked, use "Enable map view token expiration" (allow up to two weeks if it was already on).
data_description.contributor_mode: Choose how your device contributes to Google's network (All areas by default for crowdsourced reporting, or High-traffic areas only).
data_description.secrets_extra_watch_paths: Optional. Extra absolute paths to secrets.json files the integration should watch for automatic pickup, one per line. Leave empty to watch only the default locations.

rebuild_registry.description: Maintenance: Run a soft data→options migration or rebuild entities/devices for this integration. Administrators only when called by a user.

device_ids.description: Limit the operation to specific devices. Leave empty to target all Google Find My devices.

read_beacon_state.name: Read Beacon State
read_beacon_state.description: Diagnostic: connects to a tracker over Bluetooth, reads its FMDN state and returns it as the response. It sends read requests only and runs only when called; administrators only. The first access to a Provider that was never accessed before makes it choose an owner account key until factory reset, so use it on trackers that are already set up.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: Select a Google Find My device (or pass a canonical ID via Developer Tools).

address.name: Bluetooth address (optional)
address.description: Connect to this address instead of searching for a Fast Pair advertisement that matches the device's account key. The address is not checked against any key.

timeout.name: Timeout (optional)
timeout.description: Time limit in seconds, 5 to 120, for the key lookup and again for connection and reads. Cleanup may add a few seconds.

include_raw_response.name: Include raw response (optional)
include_raw_response.description: Also return the raw provisioning response as hexadecimal. It holds the tracker's full current EID, so treat the output accordingly.

search_seconds.name: EID search window (optional)
search_seconds.description: Seconds to search on each side of the tracker's clock, second by second, for the counter behind an EID. 0 turns it off. It runs after the connection has closed, adds up to 5 minutes and loads the CPU meanwhile.

search_eid.name: EID to search for (optional)
search_eid.description: An EID seen in an advertisement, 20 or 32 bytes in hexadecimal. Searched in addition to the EID the tracker reports and the EID the chosen address advertises. Used only with a search.

identity_form.name: Identity to connect to (optional)
identity_form.description: Which identity of the tracker to connect to: any, the locator that sends the FMDN frame, or the audio device that announces Common Audio. Ignored when an address is given.

derivation_windows.name: Derivation search window (optional)
derivation_windows.description: Rotation windows of 1024 s to search on each side of the tracker's clock, trying other key and block forms against the target EIDs. 0 turns it off. It runs after the connection has closed, adds up to 5 minutes and loads the CPU meanwhile.

fcm_connection_stuck.title: FCM Push Connection Failed
fcm_connection_stuck.description:
The background connection to Google is blocked.

1. Is outgoing **TCP Port 5228** allowed in your firewall?
2. If network is fine, try regenerating your `secrets.json` (credentials might be split/revoked).

fcm_reauth_required.title: Google Find My Device push needs re-authentication

confirm.title: Re-authenticate Google Find My Device
confirm.description:
The background push connection to Google failed for an extended period and could not recover on its own. This usually means the stored push credentials were revoked or rotated (for example after a Google password change, or when requests arrive from a new IP address or region). Less commonly, outgoing **TCP port 5228** is blocked by a firewall.

Select **Submit** to re-authenticate this account. Your device identity is preserved. If the problem persists afterwards, make sure port 5228 is allowed and regenerate your `secrets.json`.

abort.reauth_started: Re-authentication has been started. Finish signing in to restore the background push connection. This repair stays open until the connection recovers, so the prompt is not lost if the sign-in is interrupted.

multiple_config_entries.title: Multiple configuration entries detected
multiple_config_entries.description: Google Find My Device now supports multiple configuration entries, one per Google account. If each entry targets a different account, no action is required. When the same account is added twice, Home Assistant creates a **Duplicate account entries** repair issue for the new entry so you can remove or re-enable the correct one.

unique_id_collision.title: Entity unique ID collision detected
unique_id_collision.description:
Some entities for **{entry}** already use the new unique ID format and conflict with the migration.

**Count:** {count}
**Examples:** {entities}

To resolve:
1) Open **Settings → Devices & Services → Entities** and search for the listed entities.
2) Remove or rename conflicting entities, or delete abandoned entries from other integrations.
3) Reload the integration (or restart Home Assistant). The migration will retry automatically.

duplicate_account_entries.title: Duplicate account entries detected

cache_purged.title: Authentication cache cleared
cache_purged.description: The stored authentication cache for **{entry_title}** was unreadable and has been cleared. Select **Reconfigure** on the integration card to sign in again and restore access.

fcm_short_run_crash_loop.title: FCM Push Crash Loop Detected
fcm_short_run_crash_loop.description:
The FCM push client repeatedly disconnects within seconds of connecting (short-run crash loop). This is most often caused by a persistent poison notification on the inbound queue that cannot be decoded.

1. Reload the integration to clear the run state.
2. If the issue returns, regenerate your `secrets.json` (Google may have rotated credentials).

restart_required.title: Restart Home Assistant to finish the update
restart_required.description:
Google Find My Hub was updated on disk to version {installed_version}, but Home Assistant is still running version {running_version}. Restart Home Assistant to activate the installed version.

Reloading the integration is not enough: a full Home Assistant restart is required.

tracker_attributes_frozen.title: Tracker attributes now keep the value of the last observation

tracker_attributes_frozen_no_automations.title: Tracker attributes now keep the value of the last observation
tracker_attributes_frozen_no_automations.description:
The device trackers of **{entry_title}** no longer update the attributes `location_age` and `location_status` between observations: they keep the value of the last observation and change only with the next one (for example a new fix, the change to stale, or an availability change). The main tracker keeps the `coarse_*` attributes the same way, and the Last Location tracker no longer has them. A tracker without a new fix therefore no longer looks fresher than another one, for example to a person.

For the live values, use these entities:
{replacement_sensors}

These attributes will be removed, at the latest with the first integration release from Home Assistant {breaks_version} on.
